properties.areaDesc: Transylvania, NC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 2:00AM EDT until October 11 at 6:15AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southwestern Transylvania County in western North
Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 615 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots. Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible. A
few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible. A small
culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 153 AM EDT, Rainfall of 2 to 4 inches have fallen over the
past 12 hours. The rainfall has accumulated steadily, allowing
soils to slowly saturate and runoff to slowly increase.

Out of bank conditions will develop by area streams such as
Little River, Davidson River, and Forks of the Upper French Broad
River.

Additional rounds of showers are expected to develop over the
next few hours and the threat will persist through the early
morning hours on Sunday. These showers and storms will be very
efficient at producing heavy rainfall. Soils are saturated and
streams are swollen. Therefore, additional heavy rain may quickly
create new areas of flooding and cause previous areas of flooding
to redevelop.  As a result, Flash Flood Warnings may be issued
tonight. Caution is advised near any stream or other vulnerable
area. Seek higher ground immediately if heavy rain develops.
Please have a plan in place should flash flooding develop and do
not hesitate to act. Please heed all evacuation orders from
Emergency Management officials.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Lake Toxaway, Gorges State Park, B.R. Parkway-Black Balsam To
Mount Pisgah, Balsam Grove and Sapphire.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Only when it is safe to do so, please report flooding or landslides
threatening roads or property to the National Weather Service
Greenville-Spartanburg by calling 1...800...2 6 7...8 1 0 1, by
posting on our Facebook page, or by posting on X using hashtag
NWSGSP. Your message should describe the specific location, address,
or intersection where impacts occurred and the depth of flooding
observed.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 615 AM EDT THIS MORNING

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern San Diego County in southwestern California...

* WHEN...Until 100 AM PDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

properties.areaDesc: Henderson, NC; Transylvania, NC
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 1:54AM EDT until October 12 at 10:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued
a Flood Warning for the following rivers in North Carolina...

French Broad River at Grove Bridge Rd in Blantyre affecting
Henderson and Transylvania Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...French Broad River at Grove Bridge Rd in Blantyre.

* WHEN...From early this morning to Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Minor Flood Stage. Farmland flooding
continues on both sides of the French Broad River. Floodwaters
begin to impact boat access areas at Grove Bridge Rd. and Crab
Creek Rd.

At 17.0 feet, Minor Flooding continues.  Floodwaters continue to
inundate farmland between the French Broad River and the old
railroad bed. Floodwaters may start to inundate the shoulders of
River Road near the Big Willow Road intersection. Floodwaters
continue to impact boat access areas at Grove Bridge Rd. and Crab
Creek Rd.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 15.0 feet and rising
steadily.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 17.5 feet
later today. It will then fall below Minor Flood Stage late this
evening.
- Minor Flood Stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

For detailed information including observed and forecast stages,
flood impacts, flood history, FEMA Flood Hazard Layers, and more,
please visit: https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP

The next statement should be issued Monday morning before 1000 AM
EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT FROM EARLY THIS MORNING TO MONDAY MORNING

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 12:54AM CDT until October 13 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Aransas Islands, Kleberg Islands, Nueces Islands and
Calhoun Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 1 AM CDT Tuesday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, until 7 AM CDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the most experienced swimmers away from shore into deeper
water. These rip currents can become life-threatening to
anyone entering the surf.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
FFWPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern La Paz County in west central Arizona...
Northeastern Imperial County in southeastern California...

* Until 145 AM MST /145 AM PDT/.

* At 1049 PM MST /1049 PM PDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. The expected rainfall
rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1
to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Cibola.

properties.description:

to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal Pender and Coastal New Hanover Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 AM EDT this
morning. For the High Rip Current Risk, from 6 AM EDT this
morning through this evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
from 7 AM to 10 AM EDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Low-lying roads and locations along the Intracoastal
Waterway and adjacent tidal creeks may observe minor coastal
flooding. Check with local officials for any road closures or
impacts. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on
average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

dangerous surf conditions.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 AM EDT this
morning. For the High Rip Current Risk, from 6 AM EDT this
morning through this evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
from 7 AM to 10 AM EDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Low-lying roads and locations along the Intracoastal
Waterway and adjacent tidal creeks may observe minor coastal
flooding. Check with local officials for any road closures or
impacts. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Avery, NC; Burke, NC; Caldwell, NC
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 1:39AM EDT until October 11 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has extended
the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Avery County in western North Carolina...
Northwestern Burke County in western North Carolina...
West Central Caldwell County in western North Carolina...

* Until 400 AM EDT.

* At 139 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the warned
area. Between 4 and 6 inches of rain have fallen over the past 12
hours. Steady rises are occurring in area streams including the
Linville River, Wilson Creek, Johns River, Mulberry Creek and
Warrior Fork Creek. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,
including parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat- access
areas, and campgrounds.  Significant flooding of
poor-drainage areas are likely, impacting travel.
Low-lying roadways are likely to be flooded, requiring
barricades.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Crossnore, Table Rock, B.R. Parkway-Linville Falls To Grandfather,
Linville Falls, B.R. Parkway-Little Switzerland To Linville, Lake
James State Park, Grandfather Mountain State Park, Lake James,
Jonas Ridge and Edgemont.

Wilson Creek at Adako Rd, 3 miles southwest of Colletsville has risen
above flood stage and is still rising. Flooding of low-lying areas
adjacent to Wilson Creek is developing with lesser impacts to
vulnerable property.  More significant floodwaters are beginning to
impact low-lying areas, with inundation approximately 2-4 ft deep.
Low-water crossings may be inundated with up to 2-3 ft of
floodwaters.  Campgrounds, secondary roads, and outbuildings may be
experiencing flooding up to 1-2 ft deep.  Flooding less than 1 ft
deep may begin impacting basements and primary roads.
properties.instruction:
Only when it is safe to do so, please report flooding or landslides
threatening roads or property to the National Weather Service
Greenville-Spartanburg by calling 1...800...2 6 7...8 1 0 1, by
posting on our Facebook page, or by posting on X using hashtag
NWSGSP. Your message should describe the specific location, address,
or intersection where impacts occurred and the depth of flooding
observed.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

The additional heavy rain will increase the risk of landslides and
debris flows, especially in areas where landslides have occurred in
the past. Be especially alert if you live near a stream, particularly
at the base of a mountain or in a cove. Watch for signs that a
landslide may be imminent, including loose-moving soil and rocks or a
sudden increase in streamflow. Stay indoors and do NOT go outside to
investigate. Escape vertically inside your home by moving upstairs or
getting on top of counters to avoid being swept away.
